scope: An independent, open-ended historical essay shelf. First two essays: India 1975–1979 and South Africa 1990–1997; complete Simplified and Traditional Chinese and independently written English.
current_scope: Four essays: the original India/South Africa pair plus Germany 1933 and South Korea 1987–1988, all in three complete reading modes.
research_report_role: Case selection and research leads only; not published as a verified evidentiary source. Factual passages link to separately inspected records.
editorial_rules: No national ranking, fixed phase labels or inevitable historical sequence in the essays.
No invented dialogue, interior monologue, eyewitness detail or composite participant.
Distinguish institutional existence, access to a remedy, the decision reached and its effect.
Keep restrictions, expansions and the costs to different people visible without false equivalence.
Preserve the original eight State essays and the three fictional companion essays; do not continue their numbering.
reviewed_corrections: India: 9 May 1978 is the date of the statement of objects and reasons, not enactment of the Forty-fourth Amendment. Assent is 30 April 1979; provision-specific commencement is distinct.
India: the 27 June 1975 Article 359 order names Articles 14, 21 and 22. Do not fold Article 19's separate emergency treatment into that order.
India: distinguish the 1971 external emergency from the 1975 internal emergency and the revocation of each. The essay's 21 March 1977 date concerns the latter.
South Africa: refusal of certification is not repeal of a constitution already in force; certification applies the previously agreed Constitutional Principles.
South Africa: appointment/removal vote thresholds are not an independently sufficient or universal test of institutional independence.
South Africa: amnesty was conditional and could affect civil as well as criminal liability; a constitutional justification is not consent by every affected family.
source_access_notes: ADM Jabalpur primary judgment read in a JUDIS text mirror. The mirror is disclosed; its legacy official PDF link returns 404.

The official Bhanudas PDF was surfaced with the quoted proclamations in web search, but direct PDF loading was intermittent; no claim is made that every historical file was downloaded or independently authenticated.
The Constitutional Court archive supplies the first certification decision and text; the second certification judgment was inspected on the Justice Department's official host.
Original TRC Act government introduction and Gazette link are used instead of a guessed legacy act URL.
